title: Norfolk Island Hibiscus: Ancient Norfolk Island Hibiscuses You Can Visit
meta_description: A single-island native from the Tasman Sea, nicknamed the itchy bomb tree for its irritating seed pods, planted for salt tolerance from Setubal to Palma.
intro: Lagunaria patersonii comes from one small island in the Tasman Sea, Norfolk Island, a native range of about thirty-five square kilometres that makes almost anywhere else it grows a transplant by definition. Coastal cities plant it for a practical reason: it tolerates salt wind and poor soil better than most ornamental trees, and it flowers in summer in pale pink cups that pass for a small hibiscus. The seed pods carry the species' other reputation, packed with fine hairs that itch for hours if opened carelessly, which is why English speakers call it the itchy bomb tree. Three mapped, in Setubal, Barcelona and Palma de Mallorca.
